memories.content: The instructions for one medication the user takes say to take it after the evening meal.
On a day with a morning appointment, the user miscalculated the fasting period and checked again at the reception desk.
For an afternoon visit, the user felt less rushed while preparing to travel than for a morning visit.
On a day there was no waiting chair, the user stood for 20 minutes and their back became uncomfortable.
On a day medication instructions were explained all at once and at length, the user failed to write down an important time.
On a day medication times were confirmed one line at a time, the user copied them directly into their schedule after returning home.
On a visit when their younger brother drove them, the user did not have to find a separate route home.
The user's younger brother prefers to receive a request for weekday-afternoon transportation two days beforehand rather than on the day itself.
The local agent cannot determine the current prescription or whether use continues from medication notes alone.
The waiting area at that clinic has too few chairs, so there may be periods when people must wait standing.
The user stores wrapping paper and empty gift boxes on the upper shelf of the bedroom closet.
From photographs, the user discovered that they had given their mother the same type of kitchen item two years in a row.
This year, the user went to the market with their mother and let her choose a needed item directly.
The user once ordered a gift late and had it delivered the day after the gathering.
The next year, the user checked the expected delivery date and ordered one week before the gathering.
The user did not put names on wrapped boxes and handed their older sister and younger brother each other's gifts.
The next time the user wrapped gifts, they wrote the recipient on the bottom of each box.
The user's younger brother welcomes a snack the family can share immediately more than an item for his use alone.
The local agent can find past gift records and flag duplicates but cannot know what is needed this year.
Year-end deliveries may take longer than usual or have their expected dates changed.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate operational domains: the reference concerns medication handling, clinic visits, accessibility, and transportation, while the compared frame concerns gift selection, ordering, labeling, storage, and delivery. No claims address the same decision closely enough for a cross-frame semantic relation.
